notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This subject is mentioned briefly or beside others, so the draft is short and states only what the cited ayat state. The chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: Messengers came to Ibrahim with good news; they spoke a greeting of peace and he answered with peace.
He soon brought a roasted calf, and when he saw that their hands did not reach it, he found them strange and felt fear of them.
They told him not to fear: they had been sent to the people of Lut.
His wife was standing there and she laughed; they gave her the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Yaqub.
She said, in surprise, that she was an old woman and her husband an old man, and asked whether she could bear a child; she called it a strange thing.
They answered by asking whether she wondered at God's decree, and said that God's mercy and blessings were upon the household, for He is praiseworthy and glorious.

chapters.summary_md: Messengers came to Ibrahim and gave his wife the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Yaqub [c1][c4]. She was surprised, being an old woman with an old husband [c5]. They asked whether she wondered at God's decree [c6].
chapters.body_md:
Messengers came to Ibrahim with good news; they spoke a greeting of peace and he answered with peace [c1]. He soon brought a roasted calf, and when he saw that their hands did not reach it, he found them strange and felt fear of them [c2]. They told him not to fear: they had been sent to the people of Lut [c3].

His wife was standing there and she laughed; they gave her the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Yaqub [c4]. She said, in surprise, that she was an old woman and her husband an old man, and asked whether she could bear a child; she called it a strange thing [c5]. They answered by asking whether she wondered at God's decree, and said that God's mercy and blessings were upon the household, for He is praiseworthy and glorious [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The good news is given in parts: Ishaq first, and after Ishaq, Yaqub [c4]. The wife's surprise rests on her age and her husband's [c5]. The reply points to God's decree and to His mercy and blessings upon the household [c6].
chapters.kids_md: Visitors came to Ibrahim with good news [c1]. They told Ibrahim's wife that she would have a son called Ishaq, and after him, Yaqub [c4]. She was surprised because she was old [c5]. The visitors reminded her that this was God's decree [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the verses show surprise being answered by a reminder of God's decree [c5][c6]. Another is that the good news looks ahead past one child to the next [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the names of the visitors or how many came; the verses call them messengers and say no more.
- Not established: the name of Ibrahim's wife, or her age or his.
- Not established: where the visit took place or how long before the birth the news came.
- Not established: the relation of Yaqub to Ishaq beyond 'after Ishaq'; the verse gives the order of the news and does not name him as a son.

chapters.title_en: Given by God and made a prophet

claims.statement_en: When he withdrew from his people and from what they worshipped besides God, God granted him Ishaq and Yaqub, and made each of them a prophet.
God gave them of His mercy and gave them a high and truthful mention.
God granted him Ishaq and Yaqub as an additional gift and made each of them righteous.
God made them leaders who guide by His command, revealed to them the doing of good, the keeping up of prayer and the giving of zakat, and they were worshippers of God.
God granted him Ishaq and Yaqub, placed prophethood and the scripture among his offspring, gave him his reward in this world, and said that in the hereafter he is among the righteous.
God gave glad tidings of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous.
God blessed the one who received the tidings, and Ishaq; among the offspring of both, some do good and some clearly wrong themselves.

chapters.summary_md: God granted Ishaq and Yaqub and made each of them a prophet [c1]. God made them leaders who guide by His command [c4]. Ishaq is also given as glad tidings, a prophet from among the righteous [c6].
chapters.body_md:
When he withdrew from his people and from what they worshipped besides God, God granted him Ishaq and Yaqub, and made each of them a prophet [c1]. God gave them of His mercy and gave them a high and truthful mention [c2]. God granted him Ishaq and Yaqub as an additional gift and made each of them righteous [c3].

God made them leaders who guide by His command, revealed to them the doing of good, the keeping up of prayer and the giving of zakat, and they were worshippers of God [c4]. God granted him Ishaq and Yaqub, placed prophethood and the scripture among his offspring, gave him his reward in this world, and said that in the hereafter he is among the righteous [c5].

God gave glad tidings of Ishaq, a prophet from among the righteous [c6]. God blessed the one who received the tidings, and Ishaq; among the offspring of both, some do good and some clearly wrong themselves [c7].
chapters.deep_md: Ishaq and Yaqub are named together in most of these passages, as the gift [c1][c3][c5]. The same passages describe what God made of them: prophets [c1], righteous [c3], leaders who guide [c4]. The last passage names Ishaq alone, with glad tidings and a blessing [c6][c7], and the final verse says that the offspring of those blessed include both those who do good and those who clearly wrong themselves [c7].
chapters.kids_md: God gave Ishaq and Yaqub as a gift and made each of them a prophet [c1]. God made them leaders who guide people by His command [c4]. They worshipped God [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that these verses describe guidance as something God gives to those He makes leaders, together with prayer and good deeds [c4]. Another is that the last verse reminds readers that blessing on a line does not settle how each person in it behaves [c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who 'him' is in these passages and who 'the one who received the tidings' is in the last. The neighbouring verses, which this draft does not cite, name him, and the draft reads the pronouns that way only in this note.
- Not established: whether the passages describe one gift from different sides or separate moments.
- Not established: whether the Arabic word for 'additional gift' means a gift beyond a first request or something else; this draft keeps the plain sense.
- Not established: what the high and truthful mention was, or in whose speech.
- Not established: whether the glad tidings of Ishaq belong to the vision of a sacrifice that comes just before them. The verses do not say, and this draft does not name the son of that passage.

claims.statement_en: The hearer is told to remember God's servants Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub, who are described as people of strength and insight.
God says He made them pure by a special quality: the remembrance of the abode.
With God they are among the chosen, the best.

chapters.summary_md: God names Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub as His servants [c1]. He says they are among the chosen, the best [c3].
chapters.body_md: The hearer is told to remember God's servants Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub, who are described as people of strength and insight [c1]. God says He made them pure by a special quality: the remembrance of the abode [c2]. With God they are among the chosen, the best [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The passage groups the servants and gives them descriptions: strength and insight [c1], purity through the remembrance of the abode [c2], and being among the chosen and the best [c3].
chapters.kids_md: God asked us to remember His servants Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub [c1]. God said they are among the best [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage makes remembrance of the abode the quality for which they were singled out [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what the Arabic words rendered 'strength' and 'insight' refer to; they can be taken as actions and as vision, and this draft keeps them general.
- Not established: what 'the abode' means. It is often read as the hereafter, and this draft does not decide.
- Not established: whether the special quality is a gift to them or a thing they did.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about this prophet. None is used in this draft.
21:72: the Arabic word rendered 'an additional gift' (nafilah) is read in more than one way; the draft keeps the plain sense and a scholar should check the wording.
19:50: the phrase rendered 'a high and truthful mention' is literally 'a tongue of truth, high'; a scholar should check the wording.
38:45-46: 'strength and insight' (literally 'hands and sights') and 'the remembrance of the abode' are read in more than one way; the draft keeps them general.
37:112-113: the draft does not name the son in the vision of a sacrifice and does not say whether the tidings of Ishaq belong to that passage.
The pronoun 'him' in 19:49, 21:72, 29:27 and 37:112-113 has no named referent in the cited verses; the draft keeps the pronoun and flags it in the unknowns.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: personal names for Ishaq's wife, children, and the place and length of his life; none is used.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
